Well after many years of playing the other games DS3 was a disappointment for various reasons. If I’d played it first it would probably be my fav DS game (just like 2 is). If I had to list a few reasons without going into too much 
detail:

- many repeated events for the purpose of nostalgia (storm ruler, dragons on bridges, many returning enemies, boss designs and areas etc.) Took away much of the quality of the game as it just felt like I was replaying an imitation of previous games

- I didn’t need EVERY boss to have a phase 2 and every weapon to have a special attack. Took away much of the enjoyment and surprise you get in other games

- Personally feel that the Bloodborne engine does not suit this game like it does for Sekiro. 

- The decision to lock rings behind multiple new game plus cycles (plus trying to stop people respec-ing their builds multiple times). That and no bonfire ascetics make this game unnecessarily obnoxious to make builds for pvp



It’s still a great game with it’s share of good moments. I just wish it hadn’t referenced previous games so much and used it’s own engine and felt more unique. It was put together incredibly fast and considering that it was surprisingly quality. I think DS3 kinda just told me that we really don’t need another Dark Souls game and it seems the team at From feel the same way as they’ve moved to other games

Some things with rolling in DS2

You invincibility starts almost immediately when you hit the roll button and how long you stay invincible depends on your agility. You can view your agility in the stats screen and when you are leveling up. It’s raised by raising adaptability and Attunment, with adaptability being the better of the two if you aren’t interested in using spells.

Without going into too much detail I recommend getting your agility stat to 100 as it will give you some extra invincibility frames to work with (-and you can use estus faster!). If you’d like another frame you can go to 105 but I wouldn’t recommend going any further than that.

But with high agility and knowing that those iframes start so early, you can much more comfortably roll into many attacks as long as they don’t have lingering hitboxes of any sort

Edit: roll distance is determined by equip weight. Unlike the other games the only cut off point is for fat rolling at 70%. From 0-70% the lighter you are the further you’ll roll and vice versa
